turnaround_reason: Charter fell ~65% from ~$285 to ~$142 on relentless broadband subscriber losses (172k in Q2 2026) from fixed-wireless and fiber competition. It could re-rate if the just-closed $34.5B Cox merger delivers ~$800M synergies, mobile keeps scaling (12M lines), and broadband losses stabilize.
bullish_points: Extraordinary insider conviction: 75% net insider buying over 6 months, including CEO Winfrey buying ~$1.2M at $172
Deep value: forward P/E ~3.4, EV/EBITDA ~5.4, P/B ~1.0, with ~$2.2B FCF and ~$16.5B operating cash flow
Cox merger closed (~37M customers, largest US broadband/video); synergy target raised to $800M from $500M
Mobile is a real growth engine (12M lines) and video losses are shrinking (down ~67% YoY); heavy short interest (~34% of float) is fuel for a squeeze on any good print
bearish_points: Core broadband subs still declining — the secular question is unanswered, not resolved
Enormous leverage: ~$96.7B total debt, D/E ~442, current ratio 0.36 — little room if EBITDA slips
Fixed-wireless (T-Mobile/Verizon) and fiber overbuilders keep pressuring the moat
Cox integration is large and complex; synergy realization and churn risk are real
catalyst: Broadband net-add stabilization plus visible Cox synergy capture and continued mobile growth
catalyst_timing: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-30; Cox synergy ramp through 2027
suggested_trade: Starter spot now (small-to-medium), add on a broadband-stabilization print. Existing deep-dive in data/research/CHTR.md. LEAPS (Jan 2027/2028 calls) reasonable for a leveraged-equity re-rate given cheap IV.
key_risk: Broadband losses accelerate and pressure EBITDA against the massive debt load, so the cheap multiple stays cheap or compresses further.
would_skip_if: Q3 broadband losses widen materially or management walks back Cox synergy guidance.
